case_number: CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 923 OF 2022 (ARISING OUT OF SLP (CRL.) NO. 9470 OF 2021)
summary: The State of West Bengal appealed against the Calcutta High Court's bail order for the respondent accused under Sections 21(b)/29/27A of the NDPS Act. The prosecution alleged that the respondent financed the procurement of 76 grams of cocaine and conspired to plant it in a vehicle to frame others out of personal vendetta. Key evidence included witness statements, call records, CCTV footage, and recovery of a deleted hard disk. The High Court granted bail citing lack of direct recovery, contradictions in initial FIR and charge-sheet, and applicability of intermediate quantity thresholds under Section 37 NDPS Act. The Supreme Court, while noting the seriousness of accusations, upheld the bail considering the nature of evidence and procedural delays.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 21(b)/29/27A of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
final_judgment: Appeal dismissed; bail granted by High Court upheld with conditions.
